codearbiter.name: codeArbiter
codearbiter.eyebrow: A governance layer for AI coding agents
codearbiter.title: Let agents build. Keep the evidence.
codearbiter.summary: A repository-owned workflow for specs, decisions, tests, reviews, and durable project context. Coding agents can move fast without quietly skipping the work that makes a change trustworthy.
codearbiter.image_alt: Official codeArbiter project artwork showing its hard-gate concept
codearbiter.image_note: Project artwork from the codeArbiter repository. This is not a screenshot of a live review.
codearbiter.intro: It's knowing what happened before that code reached a branch. An agent can report success without preserving the failure it fixed, the test it ran, or the human decision it needed. codeArbiter puts those checkpoints beside the repository instead of leaving them in a transient conversation.

features.title: Work has a lane
features.text: A docs change, a regression and a security-sensitive feature follow proportionate paths, each with named evidence requirements.

features.title: The repository remembers
features.text: Specs, plans, architecture decisions, reviews and audit history live in a shared .codearbiter/ project store.

features.title: Different hosts, one record
features.text: Claude Code, Codex CLI and the Pi preview use adapters around the same repository-owned state. Host-specific support and maturity are documented separately.

decisions.label: Tradeoff 01
decisions.title: More friction where it matters
decisions.text: A hard gate can interrupt an agent. That's deliberate for missing tests, unresolved decisions and unsafe commits. Smaller changes use narrower lanes.

decisions.label: Tradeoff 02
decisions.title: Human authority stays explicit
decisions.text: The harness blocks or requests evidence; it doesn't silently approve its own exceptions, merge to the default branch, or invent an answer to a confirmation question.

codearbiter.demo_title: See how a gate changes the path
codearbiter.demo_description: Choose a kind of change. This is an explanatory simulation of workflow rules, not an invocation of a codeArbiter hook.
codearbiter.note: For a source-backed guard demonstration, see the real hook replay on the codeArbiter site.

sim.name: Service Integration Map
sim.eyebrow: Make an environment understandable before changing it
sim.title: See the services. Follow the dependencies.
sim.summary: A browser-based map for building a clearer picture of multiple networks, the services inside them, and the relationships that cross boundaries. Keep the working dataset in a local SQLite file.
sim.image_note: Fictional network illustration. The real SIM interface and demo are available through Open SIM.
sim.intro: Service inventories rarely tell the whole story. A network might provide identity, consume a shared application, or depend on an external provider. SIM makes those relationships inspectable while keeping the dataset under the person's control.

features.title: Network-aware inventory
features.text: Record networks, services, organizations, consumers, support assignments and explicit dependencies. Routes can include cross-domain solutions where recorded.

features.title: Questions become views
features.text: Trace Depends on and Used by relationships, save assessment views and capture scoped maps as PNG or SVG.

features.title: The file stays yours
features.text: The app runs without an account or backend. You open and save a local SQLite dataset; browser support determines whether saving is in place or via download.

decisions.label: Tradeoff 01
decisions.title: No invisible discovery
decisions.text: The map represents what someone has recorded. It doesn't claim unverified connections have been automatically found or validated.

decisions.label: Tradeoff 02
decisions.title: A local file is the source of truth
decisions.text: The data isn't kept in browser storage or sent to a central service. The user owns backup, handling and distribution decisions.

sim.demo_description: Select a fictional service to highlight the connections it depends on or provides. This small diagram explains how to read the relationships; the real SIM app has the editor and saved data.
sim.note: SIM is not a classification-aware system. Avoid putting sensitive or controlled information into datasets without approved handling processes.
sim.proof_label: Try the real fictional demo inside SIM

singedterra.name: singedTerra
singedterra.title: The wind changes everything.
singedterra.summary: An artillery game with terrain that remembers your shots. Aim, choose power, manage resources, and survive the consequences in local battles or supported online rooms.
singedterra.image_alt: Actual singedTerra battle HUD on the Glassstorm Expanse battlefield
singedterra.image_note: Gameplay screenshot from the project's published README.
singedterra.intro: A tribute to the turn-based artillery games where angle, wind and ammunition matter. Shots carve craters, unsupported ground falls, and the battlefield changes as the match goes on. The visual console has evolved, but the tension comes from making the shot count.

features.title: Destructible terrain
features.text: Explosions change a per-pixel terrain bitmap; craters, collapses and dirt weapons influence subsequent turns.

features.title: More than one way to play
features.text: First Salvo, CPU practice and local 2–4-seat battles are available without an account. Online rooms use a separate service.

features.title: Shared rules, reproducible outcomes
features.text: A deterministic TypeScript engine powers both hot-seat and online lockstep play; online rooms synchronize committed actions rather than streaming the whole state.

decisions.label: Tradeoff 01
decisions.title: Simulation belongs to the shared engine
decisions.text: A single engine defines physics and turns. The Canvas renderer is presentation and can't change a match result.

decisions.label: Tradeoff 02
decisions.title: Keep verification honest
decisions.text: Online verified achievements require actual backend verification; local and unavailable trials never invent a verified result.

singedterra.demo_description: Adjust elevation, power and crosswind to see an approximate trajectory change. This is a teaching illustration, not the singedTerra engine or a guaranteed shot predictor.
singedterra.note: The game runs in your browser. Casual local play needs no sign-in; online rooms use Supabase.
singedterra.proof_label: Read how the deterministic engine works

meridian.name: Meridian
meridian.eyebrow: A browser studio for Mermaid diagrams
meridian.title: Make a diagram worth presenting.
meridian.summary: Write Mermaid with a live preview, style the diagram on the canvas, and use scenes to walk an audience through it. Export a static image, a project file, or a self-contained HTML presentation.
meridian.image_alt: The Meridian editor showing the Edge to cloud diagram with Mermaid source beside the canvas
meridian.image_note: The Edge to cloud example in Meridian.
meridian.intro_title: A working diagram often needs a second pass.
meridian.intro: Mermaid makes it easy to keep a diagram beside the system it describes. When it comes time to explain that system, Meridian gives the same diagram a canvas for adjusting how it looks and deciding what to show first.

features.title: Edit the source live
features.text: Update Mermaid beside the canvas. The last good diagram stays visible when the text is temporarily incomplete.

features.title: Work through it in scenes
features.text: Use visibility, highlights and connector motion to focus each step of a presentation.

features.title: Take the project with you
features.text: Download editable project JSON, SVG or PNG images, or a standalone HTML presentation.

decisions.label: Tradeoff 01
decisions.title: Keep the Mermaid text readable
decisions.text: Canvas styling and storyboard scenes are stored separately from the source, so the Mermaid text stays ready to reuse elsewhere.

decisions.label: Tradeoff 02
decisions.title: Keep authoring local
decisions.text: The studio runs in the browser without an account. The workspace stays in browser storage, and a downloaded project file is a portable backup.

meridian.demo_title: Read the source behind the diagram
meridian.demo_description: The example connects a field endpoint through an edge gateway to four core services. Open its Mermaid source below, then load Edge to cloud from Browse examples to edit it yourself.
meridian.note: The example is built into the studio.
